elaine: Heads-up: following up on the airgap hotswap controller RFC — want to lock down controller/operator contract before next sprint.

mike: Quick Q: is the controller responsible for signature verification, or do we rely on verifier sidecar? I prefer minimal controller surface.

sanjay: Prefer verifier sidecar. Controller should only orchestrate swap state machine + retries. Sidecar/agent does heavy crypto and blob streaming.

elaine: Agreed. Main constraints: air-gapped nodes can't pull from registry; controller must accept pre-staged bundles via admin-provided path. Need idempotent apply and resumable state.

kevin: Operator UX question: how do we signal 'do not activate yet' during canary? We need holdback annotations and a lightweight 'preview' phase in the CR.

mike: Propose states: PRELOAD -> VERIFY -> PREVIEW -> ACTIVATE. Controller stores state on-disk tombstone so resume works after power loss.

sanjay: Concern: PRELOAD may require large disk IO. We should allow streaming verification (verify-as-we-write) to avoid full duplicate storage and speed up validation. Example CLI usage: 

```bash
# pre-stage bundle (from airgap media)
rwdctl bundle upload --node node-1 --path /mnt/usb/bundle.v1.tar
# trigger preload + verify
rwdctl bundle preload --node node-1 --bundle bundle.v1
```

elaine: Nice. Also: signature verification must be deterministic and fast — use batch hashing and early-fail on missing signer chain. Keep the controller logic: accept signed manifest + proof, hand off heavy verify to sidecar when available.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: detected test cluster preload succeeded on staging-2 (node-3). logs: preload 14m, verify 2m, preview diff ok :white_check_mark:

kevin: Edge case: interrupted activation during powercut — controller must record activation-phase id and resume leader-only ops; plan: activation lease with TTL so only one controller continues active rollout.

mike: Tradeoff: activation lease implies clock sync requirement; alternative is monotonic activation counter persisted to disk and compared on resume to avoid relying on wall clock.

sanjay: Also need explicit rollback contract: controller should keep previous active pointers until activation confirms success. On fail, operator can run `rwdctl bundle force-rollback` which uses the preserved pointers.

elaine: Action items: (1) draft small API spec for controller-state endpoints (GET /state, POST /actions), (2) add flags for streaming-verify and activation-lease in operator CRD, (3) write runbook for interrupted-activation and failure modes. I'll open a PR with spec today.

kevin: :thumbsup: I'll own the runbook. @mike can you take the CRD draft?

mike: Yep. Will post CRD diff in this channel tomorrow and link a small test harness for streaming-verify.

elaine: Thanks — aim to have the contract signed off before next arch sync.
